title: Film 1: Why am I always tired?

lines.text: Always tired? Check these three things first.
lines.tts: Always tired? Check these three things first.

lines.text: One: short sleep. All day, a chemical called adenosine builds up in your brain and makes you sleepy.
lines.tts: One: short sleep. All day, a chemical called adenosine builds up in your brain, and makes you sleepy.

lines.text: Sleep clears it. Cut sleep short, and some is left when you wake.
lines.tts: Sleep clears it. Cut sleep short, and some is left when you wake.

lines.text: Two: late coffee. Coffee doesn't clear that chemical. It hides it, and that cuts into your sleep.
lines.tts: Two: late coffee. Coffee doesn't clear that chemical. It hides it, and that cuts into your sleep.

lines.text: A coffee at six p.m.? About half of it is still in you at eleven.
lines.tts: A coffee at six p.m.? About half of it is still in you at eleven.

lines.text: Three: late light. Bright light at night, even room light, tells your body clock it's still day,
lines.tts: Three: late light. Bright light at night, even room light, tells your body clock it's still day,

lines.text: so your sleep signal comes later.
lines.tts: so your sleep signal comes later.

lines.text: For a seven a.m. alarm: in bed by eleven, last coffee by two, lights low from eight.
lines.tts: For a seven a.m. alarm: in bed by eleven, last coffee by two, lights low from eight.

lines.text: Still tired with enough sleep? See a doctor: low iron or your thyroid can cause it.
lines.tts: Still tired with enough sleep? See a doctor. Low iron, or your thyroid, can cause it.
